public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Komlós conjecture

The Komlós conjecture in discrepancy theory: there is a universal constant $K$ such
that for all $n, m$ and all vectors $v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with
$\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$, there exist signs $\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$$\left\|\sum\_{i=1}^n \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le K.$$

For a long time the best known bound was due to Banaszczyk, who proved that one can always
achieve $O(\sqrt{\log n})$. The Beck–Fiala theorem on the discrepancy of sparse set systems
is a special case (up to scaling), and the conjecture implies the Beck–Fiala
conjecture that set systems of degree $t$ have discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$.

The conjecture was proved in September 2026 by Guo, Fang and Lu with $K = 3\sqrt{2\pi}$.
Karingula and Lovett gave an elementary proof with $K = 36$. A formalisation of their proof is
recorded in the `formal_proof` attributes below.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrepancy_theory#Major_open_problems)
- [W. Banaszczyk, *Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies*,
  Random Structures & Algorithms **12** (1998), 351–360](https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1098-2418(199807)12:4%3C351::AID-RSA3%3E3.0.CO;2-S)
- [J. Spencer, *Six standard deviations suffice*,
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **289** (1985), 679–706](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1985-0784009-0)
- [S. Guo, E. X. Fang and J. Lu, *Vector balancing via directional total variation*,
  arXiv:2609.11189](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11189)
- [S. R. Karingula and S. Lovett, *An elementary proof of the Komlós conjecture*,
  arXiv:2609.20979](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20979)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace KomlosConjecture

/--
**The Komlós conjecture**

There exists a universal constant $K > 0$ such that for all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and
all vectors $v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$ (encoded here as
$\sum\_j v\_{ij}^2 \le 1$), there exist signs $\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left\|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le K$, i.e.
$\left|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_{ij}\right| \le K$ for every coordinate $j$.

Proved by Guo, Fang and Lu with $K = 3\sqrt{2\pi}$ and by Karingula and Lovett with $K = 36$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/416b6597cb193b6745748fdfef0d64342c71dae9/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/KomlosConjecture.lean#L64"]
theorem komlos_conjecture :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (n m : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ i, ∑ j, (v i j) ^ 2 ≤ 1) →
      ∃ ε : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
        ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ K := by
  sorry

/--
**Banaszczyk's theorem**

There exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and all vectors
$v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$, there exist signs
$\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left\|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le C \sqrt{\log(n + 2)}$.
This was the best known bound towards the Komlós conjecture before its solution. (The shift
$n + 2$ inside the logarithm is a harmless normalization keeping it positive for
$n \in \{0, 1\}$.) It follows from the Komlós conjecture with $C = 36 / \sqrt{\log 2}$.

[W. Banaszczyk, *Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies*,
Random Structures & Algorithms **12** (1998), 351–360.]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/416b6597cb193b6745748fdfef0d64342c71dae9/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/KomlosConjecture.lean#L86"]
theorem komlos_conjecture.variants.banaszczyk :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n m : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ i, ∑ j, (v i j) ^ 2 ≤ 1) →
      ∃ ε : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
        ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ C * Real.sqrt (Real.log (n + 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: with no vectors at all ($n = 0$), the empty signed sum is $0$ in every
coordinate, so any constant bound holds.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem komlos_conjecture.variants.zero_vectors (m : ℕ) (v : Fin 0 → Fin m → ℝ) :
    ∃ ε : Fin 0 → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
      ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ 1 :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, by simp⟩

end KomlosConjecture

findings.description: The docstring says: "This was the best known bound towards the Komlós conjecture before its solution." That is false. Banaszczyk's O(√log n) bound was improved to Õ((log n)^{1/4}) by Bansal and Jiang (arXiv:2508.03961, v1 5 Aug 2025, STOC 2026). Ercan then improved it to O((log n)^{1/4}) (arXiv:2609.08885, 8 Sep 2026), two days before Guo–Fang–Lu's proof. The Lean statement is still a true and faithful formalization of Banaszczyk's bound, so only the historical remark is wrong. The module docstring's wording, "For a long time the best known bound was due to Banaszczyk", is accurate.
findings.source_evidence: Karingula–Lovett, arXiv:2609.20979, §1 'Progress toward the conjecture': "Bansal and Jiang obtained the first asymptotic improvement over Banaszczyk's bound, proving O((log n)^{1/4}(log log n)^{7/4}). Ercan subsequently removed the iterated-logarithmic factor, obtaining O((log n)^{1/4})." Guo–Fang–Lu, arXiv:2609.11189, §1.1: "Bansal and Jiang establish the Komlós bound Õ((log n)^{1/4})". Bansal–Jiang abstract (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03961): "For the Komlos problem, we give an Õ(log^{1/4} n) bound, improving upon the previous O(√log n) bound [Random Struct. Algor., 1998]."
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: "This was the best known bound towards the Komlós conjecture from 1998 until Bansal and Jiang's $\widetilde O((\log n)^{1/4})$ bound (arXiv:2508.03961, STOC 2026). Ercan sharpened it to $O((\log n)^{1/4})$ (arXiv:2609.08885) shortly before the conjecture was proved."

reformulations.difference: The vectors are stored as coordinate arrays `v : Fin n → Fin m → ℝ`. The hypothesis ‖v_i‖₂ ≤ 1 is written `∑ j, v i j ^ 2 ≤ 1`, and ‖∑ ε_i v_i‖_∞ ≤ K is written coordinatewise as `∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ K`. n and m range over ℕ including 0, whereas Karingula–Lovett and Guo–Fang–Lu quantify over positive integers n, d.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If n = 0 the signed sum is empty, so every coordinate is 0 ≤ K. If m = 0 there are no coordinates. So allowing 0 adds only trivially true cases. √(∑ x_j²) ≤ 1 ⟺ ∑ x_j² ≤ 1, and for K ≥ 0 the sup norm on `Fin m → ℝ` is ≤ K iff every |coordinate| ≤ K. Proved in Lean (scratch files, standard axioms only): `KomlosLean ↔ KomlosSource`, the version with 0 < n and 0 < m, and `KomlosLean ↔ KomlosNorm`, the version with `v i : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`, `‖v i‖ ≤ 1` and the Mathlib sup norm of `fun j => ∑ i, ε i * v i j`. `example : KomlosLean := komlos_conjecture` checks that my definition is the file's statement.

reformulations.difference: The literature's asymptotic 'O(√log n)' becomes an explicit `∃ C > 0, ∀ n m v, … ≤ C * √(log (n + 2))`, where n is the number of vectors. Banaszczyk's paper directly gives O(√log m) in the dimension m. The bound in n, uniform in m, needs a short extra reduction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Normalization, proved in Lean (`ban_iff`, standard axioms only): '∃ C>0 ∀ n ≥ 0: disc ≤ C√log(n+2)' ⟺ '∃ C>0 ∀ n ≥ 2: disc ≤ C√log n'. For n ≥ 2, log(n+2) ≤ 2 log n. For n ≤ 1 the discrepancy is ≤ 1, since |v_ij| ≤ 1. (2) The bound in n, uniform in m, is the standard 'refined Komlós consequence' of Banaszczyk's theorem. GFL §1.1 states it explicitly; DGLN19 derives O(√log d) with d ≤ min{m,n}. Karingula–Lovett's footnote gives the reduction: rows with ‖r‖₁ ≤ 1 contribute ≤ 1 under any signing, and fewer than n² rows remain. So the Lean states a true theorem, the one the literature calls Banaszczyk's O(√log n) bound. I also proved in Lean that the file's Komlós statement implies this variant with C = K/√log 2, as the docstring says.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. All three declarations state what the sources state. I proved the equivalences listed under reformulations in Lean scratch files, using only the standard axioms, and checked that any valid K must be at least 1, so the conjecture is not trivially true.

Smaller points that are not findings:
- The module docstring says \"The Beck–Fiala theorem ... is a special case (up to scaling)\". Strictly, the Beck–Fiala *setting* is the special case. The Komlós bound K√t does not literally imply the 2t−1 bound at t = 1.
- For the conjecture itself, the file cites Spencer's 1985 \"Six standard deviations suffice\". Karingula–Lovett attribute the recording of the conjecture to Spencer's 1987 \"Ten Lectures on the Probabilistic Method\". This is a reference choice, not an error.
- The cited Wikipedia section still lists the Komlós conjecture as open. Wikipedia is stale here; the file's `research solved` tag follows the September 2026 arXiv proofs.
- Outside this file: `BeckFiala.beck_fiala_conjecture` in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/BeckFialaConjecture.lean is still tagged `research open`, although Guo–Fang–Lu's Corollary 1.2 (disc < 3√(2πt)) now settles it. I did not report this under status_issues because it belongs to another file.
